metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently underestimates sharp upward moves, especially after low-price periods; adjust forecast upward by 5–15% for sudden spikes.
- Overestimates downward trends after recent highs; apply downward bias correction only if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias; increase forecast volatility or add 3–7% upward drift for next 3–5 days.
- Overshoots after initial spikes (e.g., 40–50% above true value in first 3–5 days); cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- If true outcome shows mean-reversion within 7–10 days, model fails to correct; add 2–5% downward adjustment in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true volatility; increase standard deviation by 10–20% for high-sentiment or event-driven periods.
- If sentiment history is all 0.00, model should not assume trend continuation; instead, forecast should be centered around 3–5-day moving average of recent 10–15 days.
